relevance_reason: This paper identifies the PAK2 variant that causes KNO2 in the original KNO2 family and includes functional data on the variant.

findings.statement: Antonarakis et al. (2021) restudied a pedigree first published in 1998 and designated KNO2. Two affected sibs, born to unaffected parents, had Knobloch type 2 syndrome with intellectual disability, autistic behavior, retinal degeneration, and encephalocele.
quotes: We studied an historical pedigree (published in 1998) designated as KNO2 (Knobloch type 2 syndrome with intellectual disability, autistic behavior, retinal degeneration, encephalocele).

findings.statement: In the 2 affected sibs of the KNO2 family, Antonarakis et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing of the sibs and their unaffected parents to identify a heterozygous missense variant in PAK2, p.(Glu435Lys). The variant was apparently de novo in both sibs, which suggested germline mosaicism in one parent, but deep sequencing of the parents' blood DNA did not detect mosaicism. The variant lies in the kinase domain, and structural analysis predicted that it might compromise kinase activity.
quotes: Whole exome sequencing of the two affected siblings and the normal parents resulted in the identification of a PAK2 non-synonymous substitution p.(Glu435Lys) as a causative variant.

The variant was monoallelic and apparently de novo in both siblings indicating a likely germ-line mosaicism in one of the parents; the mosaicism, however, could not be observed after deep sequencing of blood parental DNA.
Structural analysis of the PAK2 p.(Glu435Lys) variant that is located in the kinase domain of the protein predicts a possible compromise in the kinase activity.

findings.statement: In functional studies in transfected HEK293T cells, Antonarakis et al. (2021) found that the PAK2 p.(Glu435Lys) variant caused a partial loss of kinase activity.
quotes: Functional analysis of the p.(Glu435Lys) PAK2 variant in transfected HEK293T cells results in a partial loss of the kinase activity.

findings.statement: Antonarakis et al. (2021) concluded that, unlike the autosomal recessive COL18A1-related Knobloch syndrome, KNO2 in the family they studied is a dominant disorder. Both affected sibs carried the PAK2 variant on one allele, and it was apparently de novo, which pointed to likely parental germline mosaicism.
quotes: We conclude that the KNO2 syndrome in the studied family is dominant and caused by a deleterious variant in the PAK2 gene.

findings.statement: Antonarakis et al. (2021) noted that Knobloch syndrome is usually an autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic COL18A1 variants. However, some clinically diagnosed patients have an unknown molecular cause that is not linked to COL18A1.
quotes: However, there are patients clinically diagnosed as Knobloch syndrome with unknown molecular etiology not linked to COL18A1.

relevance_reason: This paper defines the KNO2 locus: in a New Zealand Knobloch syndrome family, linkage to COL18A1 was excluded and COL15A1 was ruled out by mutation analysis.

findings.statement: Menzel et al. (2004) studied a Knobloch syndrome family from New Zealand and excluded linkage to the COL18A1 locus on 21q22.3. They took this as evidence for a second Knobloch syndrome locus, which they named KNO2.
quotes: Linkage to the COL18A1 locus was excluded in the New Zealand family, providing evidence for the existence of a second KNO locus.
We named the second unmapped locus for Knobloch syndrome KNO2.

findings.statement: In the New Zealand family with Knobloch syndrome 2, Menzel et al. (2004) used mutation analysis to exclude COL15A1 as the cause of KNO2. COL15A1 belongs to the same multiplexin collagen subfamily as COL18A1.
quotes: Mutation analysis excluded COL15A1, a member of the multiplexin collagen subfamily similar to COL18A1, as being responsible for KNO2.

findings.statement: Menzel et al. (2004) described Knobloch syndrome as an autosomal recessive disorder with high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment, and congenital encephalocele.
quotes: Knobloch syndrome (KNO) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment, and congenital encephalocele.

findings.statement: In a Hungarian family with Knobloch syndrome, Menzel et al. (2004) identified two COL18A1 mutations. One was a 1-bp insertion causing a frameshift and a premature stop codon. The other was a missense variant, D1437N (D104N in endostatin), at a conserved residue. The endostatin N104 mutant had reduced affinity for laminin, and the authors concluded that it likely represents a pathogenic mutation.
quotes: Two COL18A1 mutations were identified in the Hungarian family: a 1-bp insertion causing a frameshift and a premature in-frame stop codon and an amino acid substitution.
D1437N (D104N in endostatin) likely represents a pathogenic mutation, as we show that the endostatin N104 mutant is impaired in its affinity towards laminin.

relevance_reason: Clinical case report of two sibs with Knobloch syndrome (abstract only). No gene or variant data, so it cannot be assigned to a specific Knobloch locus.

findings.statement: Wilson et al. (1998) reported 2 sibs with Knobloch syndrome. Both had high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration, and either an occipital encephalocele or a scalp lesion. One sib had very early onset of severe eye disease. The other was notable for a very mild scalp defect. Both sibs also appeared to have an unusual pulmonary lymphatic condition.
quotes: We report on two sibs with high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration (VRD), and occipital encephalocoele or scalp lesion.
One case presents with very early onset of severe eye disease, whereas the other is notable for the very mild scalp defect.
In addition, both appear to have an unusual pulmonary lymphatic condition.

findings.statement: Wilson et al. (1998) reviewed the literature on Knobloch syndrome and discussed possible causes. They suggested that mesoderm might be involved in the morphogenesis of the disorder.
quotes: We review the literature on Knobloch syndrome, discuss possible causes, and suggest a possible involvement of mesoderm in the morphogenesis.
